name: TextAttack
hook: NLP adversarial-attack framework from the QData lab (ACL 2020).
what_atr_did: Issue #824 proposes a textattack-detection-atr companion PyPI package — plugin-shaped, zero core changes. Single ask: README cross-link.

name: Microsoft PyRIT
hook: The toolkit Microsoft uses internally to red-team production LLM products. Roman Lutz leads.
what_atr_did: Added an ATR dataset loader exposing the rule corpus as PyRIT attack sources; PR #1715 merged 2026-05-27.

name: HackAPrompt
org: Schulhoff et al. — Learn Prompting · EMNLP 2023
hook: Crowd-sourced prompt-injection competition corpus: players try to make a model print a target phrase or give up a hidden secret key.
what_atr_did: Shipped 5 ATR rules (ATR-2026-00452..00456), promoted to rules/ on 2026-05-12, each written for an attack family the corpus shows: a forced target phrase, secret-key reveal demands, per-character backslash encoding, a no-period output modifier, and empty-input conditionals. Each rule's description names HackAPrompt. Rules were written from this corpus, so recall measured on it is partly in-sample, not a measure of generalisation. The corpus is 100% adversarial and carries no benign population, so it yields no precision or false-positive figure.

name: Promptfoo + llm-guard
hook: Attack examples from promptfoo's red-team plugins and from llm-guard's test corpus.
what_atr_did: Shipped 6 ATR rules (ATR-2026-00500..00505), promoted to rules/ on 2026-05-12. Four are generalised from promptfoo plugin corpora (SSRF, data exfiltration, divergent repetition, tool discovery) and two from the llm-guard test corpus (fake error-state takeover, and system prompt extraction, which also draws on promptfoo): literal hostnames, URLs, words and tool names in the examples were replaced with patterns. Each rule's description names the corpus it came from.

name: OWASP LLM Top 10 + MITRE ATLAS
hook: OWASP's Top 10 risks for LLM applications, and MITRE ATLAS, the catalog of adversarial techniques and case studies against AI systems.
what_atr_did: Shipped 8 ATR rules (ATR-2026-00510..00517) on 2026-05-12. Each rule's references name an OWASP LLM Top 10 (2025) category (LLM01, LLM02, LLM06 or LLM10) and a MITRE ATLAS technique, and six of the eight descriptions cite the ATLAS case study they follow (AML.CS0022, CS0036, CS0038, CS0039 and CS0045, CS0041, CS0056).

name: Promptfoo
hook: Open-source LLM red-teaming and evaluation tool. Promptfoo generates and runs adversarial tests against LLM applications.
what_atr_did: PR #8529 adds an MCP red-team example using ATR as the deterministic defense layer. Promptfoo runs the probe; ATR rules return the verdict.
